page.title: Discord Bot
page.description: Manage your Discord bot, slash commands, and event notifications

setup.title: Discord Bot Setup
setup.description: Let's get your Discord bot up and running — follow the steps below

step0.heading: Create a Discord Application
step0.subheading: First, you need to create an application on Discord's Developer Portal. This only takes a minute.
step0.step1Desc: Click the button below to open it in a new tab.
step0.step2Desc: It's in the top-right corner. Name it anything you like (e.g. "PZ Server Bot").
step0.step3Desc: In the left sidebar of your new application, click Bot. Discord may auto-create a bot user, or you may see an "Add Bot" button — click it if so.
step0.whyBotTitle: Why do I need a bot?
step0.whyBotDesc: A Discord bot lets your panel send messages, register slash commands, and bridge in-game chat to a Discord channel. It runs through this panel, so you do not need separate hosting.

step1.heading: Copy Your Bot Token
step1.subheading: On the Bot page in the Developer Portal, click "Reset Token" (or "Copy" if visible), then paste it below.
step1.warningDesc: Discord only shows the token once after you reset it. If you lose it, you will need to generate a new one. Treat it like a password and never share it publicly.

step2.heading: Enable Privileged Intents
step2.subheading: Still on the Bot page in the Developer Portal, scroll down to "Privileged Gateway Intents" and enable these:
step2.serverMembersIntentWhy: Required to check user roles for admin commands
step2.messageContentIntentWhy: Required for two-way chat bridge (Discord ↔ Game)
step2.saveNoticeDesc: After toggling the intents on, scroll down and click the Save Changes button on the Discord page.

step3.heading: Invite the Bot to Your Discord Server
step3.subheadingReady: Click the button below to invite your bot. Select your Discord server from the dropdown, then click "Authorize".
step3.subheadingNotReady: We need your bot token to generate an invite link. Go back to Step 1 and paste + verify your token first, or use the manual method below.
step3.permissionsIncluded: Permissions included: Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, Use Slash Commands
step3.manualInviteDesc: If you have not verified your token yet, you can still invite the bot manually.
step3.oauthStep1: In the Developer Portal, go to your app → OAuth2 → URL Generator
step3.oauthStep3: Under "Bot Permissions", check Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, Use Slash Commands
step3.oauthStep4: Copy the generated URL at the bottom and open it in your browser
step3.oauthStep5: Select your Discord server and click Authorize
step3.backTipStep: Tip: go back to Step 1 and verify your token — we'll generate the invite link automatically.

step4.heading: Configure Server IDs
step4.subheading: The bot needs your Discord server's ID to register slash commands. You can also set a notification channel and an admin role.
step4.developerModeStep1: Open Discord → User Settings (gear icon, bottom-left)
step4.developerModeTip: Now you can right-click servers, channels, and roles to see a "Copy ID" option.
step4.guildIdHint: Right-click your Discord server name → Copy Server ID
step4.guildIdError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number
step4.channelIdHint: Right-click a text channel → Copy Channel ID. Used for notifications and two-way chat bridge.
step4.channelIdError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number
step4.adminRoleHint: Right-click a role → Copy Role ID. Only users with this role can use bot commands. Leave blank to allow everyone.
step4.adminRoleError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number

step5.heading: Ready to Launch!
step5.subheading: Review your configuration below, then save and start the bot.
step5.autoStartDesc: Automatically start the Discord bot when the panel launches

whatYouGet.title: What does the bot do?
whatYouGet.slashCommandsDesc: Control your PZ server from Discord with /status, /players, /start, /stop, /restart, /broadcast, /kick, and /rcon.
whatYouGet.chatBridgeDesc: Keep Discord and in-game chat in the same loop without switching tools during live admin work.
whatYouGet.notificationsDesc: Send join/leave, start/stop, restart, death, and backup events straight to the channel your admins already watch.

botStatus.title: Bot Status
botStatus.statusDesc: Notifications, slash commands, and the chat bridge all depend on the bot staying connected to the configured channel.

commandPermissions.title: Command Permissions
commandPermissions.description: Control who can use each slash command. Assign a permission tier per command.

configuration.title: Bot Configuration
configuration.guildIdError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit server ID
configuration.channelIdError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit channel ID

configuration.adminRoleError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit role ID
configuration.modRoleHint: Can use "moderator" tier commands. Without a configured role, role-protected commands remain locked.

chatRelay.title: Chat Relay
chatRelay.description: Bridge chat both ways between the game server and Discord
chatRelay.publicScope: All public chat (General, Say, Local, Shout)
chatRelay.scopeHint: Faction, safehouse, radio and admin chat are never forwarded. Build 42 records ordinary talking as Say, so "General tab only" relays very little.
chatRelay.scopeWarning: Local chat is forwarded to Discord. Choose General tab only to keep player proximity chat private.
chatRelay.channelHint: Relay game chat and Discord messages through a separate channel. Leave empty to use the main channel above.
chatRelay.channelPlaceholder: Leave empty to use main channel
chatRelay.channelError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit channel ID

events.title: Event Notifications
events.description: Automatic notifications posted to your Discord channel when server events occur

fieldHelp.botToken: The secret token for your bot application, copied from the Discord Developer Portal's Bot page.
fieldHelp.botTokenContext: Anyone who has this token can fully control the bot. Without it, the panel cannot log in to Discord — commands, notifications, and chat relay all stay offline.
fieldHelp.guildId: The Discord server (guild) ID the bot registers slash commands and roles for.
fieldHelp.guildIdContext: Slash commands are registered per-server. A missing or wrong Guild ID means /status, /restart, and the rest never show up in your server.
fieldHelp.channelId: The text channel used for event notifications and the two-way chat bridge.
fieldHelp.channelIdContext: Leave this blank to skip notifications and chat bridging — slash commands still work without it. Right-click a channel with Developer Mode on to copy its ID.
fieldHelp.adminRoleId: Discord role granted full access to role-protected bot commands.
fieldHelp.adminRoleIdContext: Leave blank and every member can run admin-tier commands like /restart and /rcon. Server owners and Discord Administrators always retain access regardless of this setting.
fieldHelp.modRoleId: Discord role granted access to moderator-tier commands.
fieldHelp.modRoleIdContext: Without a configured role, any command set to the moderator tier stays locked to admins only — nobody else can use it.
fieldHelp.autoStart: Start the Discord bot automatically whenever the panel launches.
fieldHelp.autoStartContext: Turn this off to start the bot manually each session — useful while testing a new token or intent change.
fieldHelp.chatRelay: Bridges chat both directions between the game server and the Discord channel.
fieldHelp.chatRelayContext: Requires the Message Content Intent enabled on the bot in the Developer Portal, or Discord messages sent by players never reach the game.
fieldHelp.chatRelayScope: Which in-game chat tabs get forwarded to Discord.
fieldHelp.chatRelayScopeContext: Faction, safehouse, radio, and admin chat are never forwarded regardless of this setting. Broader scopes expose more of players' conversations in your Discord server.
fieldHelp.chatRelayChannelId: Optional separate channel for the chat bridge, distinct from the notification channel.
fieldHelp.chatRelayChannelIdContext: Leave empty to relay chat through the main notification channel configured above.
fieldHelp.commandPermissions: Minimum permission tier required to run each slash command.
fieldHelp.commandPermissionsContext: Destructive commands like /restart, /stop, and /rcon default to Admin. Loosening a tier lets more Discord members run that command against your live server.
fieldHelp.botStatus: Live connection state of the bot process running inside the panel.
fieldHelp.botStatusContext: "Offline" with a token already configured usually means an invalid or revoked token, a missing privileged intent, or a crashed bot process — check the error box below if one appears.
fieldHelp.webhookTemplate: The message text posted to Discord when this event fires.
fieldHelp.webhookTemplateContext: Supports the variables listed below the box. An enabled event with a blank template falls back to the default wording instead of sending an empty message.

confirmDialog.wipeDescription: This clears the saved bot token, guild and channel IDs, role IDs, chat relay settings, command permissions, and Discord event notification setup. The bot will stop and the page will return to first-time setup.
